newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel destroys Arab West Bank house.
newsitem.headline: Israel destroys Arab West Bank house.

text.p: Just days after Faed Jaradat moved into his new house, Israeli soldiers threw him, his children and his furniture out on the street on Tuesday and razed the house to the ground.
Unemployed, he has nowhere to go.

"Now I have to find a tent to live in -- me and my kids. I am a refugee now. This house cost me 25,000 Jordanian dinars ($35,260). I worked for more than 10 years to get the money to build my only home," he said.
Jaradat, 28, said the army arrived in the morning and told him to take his furniture out of his two-storey house so they could tear it down.
"It was a house that was built illegally without permits and it was demolished this morning," said Peter Lerner, spokesman for Israel's military-run Civil Administration in the West Bank.
Jaradat said he built despite being denied a permit for his now-flattened home in Ardessa, near the bypass road to the Jewish settlement Kiryat Arba.
"They said, 'It's an agricultural area, you can't build here'," Jaradat said.
Lerner said most of the homes the civil administration destroys are empty, though five people had just moved into this one.
On Monday, the municipality of Jerusalem destroyed three Arab houses it said were illegally built, and Israel's Civil Administration destroyed two more in the West Bank.
Two more West Bank houses were due to be demolished on Tuesday.
The Civil Administration has destroyed 50 houses this year, all of them Palestinian, Lerner said. Last year, it destroyed 140 houses it said were illegally built.
Palestinians say Israel will not give them building permits. Israel says Palestinians don't get permits because they don't apply for them.
